sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate faithfully encodes the complete Complex Readiness contract: it targets the individual ship, preserves the Ke-or-RCH alternative with the declared units and quantity structure, requires calculation or model-test evidence, and consistently represents approval as true while permitting an approved or revoked lifecycle state. No required semantic obligation or declared contract field is omitted, and no vocabulary repair is needed.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the approval/revocation semantics. sh:class nltl:evidenceState on approvalRevocationStatus is presence-only and permits draft, submitted, under-review, rejected, expired, or revoked states, so it does not faithfully encode that the alternative Ke/RCH determination is approved while remaining revocable. Constrain the status to the applicable canonical controlled values and make its relationship with approvalStatus consistent. Preserve the existing ship target, Ke/RCH alternative, required evidence boundary, datatypes, and units.

Repair the approval-state logic while preserving the existing ship target, Ke/RCH alternative, evidence boundary, datatypes, and units. The unconditional approvalStatus sh:hasValue true conflicts with the second sh:or branch requiring approvalStatus false and makes the revoked branch impossible. Encode approvalStatus consistently as true for the granted approval, with approvalRevocationStatus constrained to either evidenceStateApproved or evidenceStateRevoked; remove the contradictory false branch (or otherwise model revocation without allowing an unapproved alternative). Keep both approved and revoked as permitted current lifecycle states, since the requirement allows approval to be revoked.

The candidate faithfully encodes the complete Complex Readiness contract: it targets the individual ship, preserves the Ke-or-RCH alternative with the declared units and quantity structure, requires calculation or model-test evidence, and consistently represents approval as true while permitting an approved or revoked lifecycle state. No required semantic obligation or declared contract field is omitted, and no vocabulary repair is needed.
